mainTopic: ברכות over fragrance, the sayings of רב זוטרא בר טוביה, the order of blessings over oil, myrtle and wine, and conduct unbecoming a תלמיד חכם
overview: The amud opens by listing which ברכה to say over different fragrances. Woody plants get בורא עצי בשמים, soft plants get בורא עשבי בשמים, and fragrant fruits like an אתרוג get הנותן ריח טוב בפירות. It also brings רב יהודה's ברכה over blossoming trees in ניסן, and רב's source for blessing over scent: 'כל הנשמה תהלל יה', because scent is the pleasure of the נשמה. A series of sayings from רב זוטרא בר טוביה follows. They include the future fragrance of the young men of ישראל, each person loving his own trade, and a torch counting like two people and the moon like three, including the walker. The series ends with the teaching that it is better to be thrown into a furnace than to shame someone in public, learned from תמר. Next, ברייתות discuss the order of ברכות over oil and myrtle, where the הלכה follows רבן גמליאל and oil comes first, and over oil and wine. Finally, a ברייתא lists things unbecoming for a תלמיד חכם, and the גמרא explains and limits each one.

steps.title: Jasmine gets the blessing for fragrant trees
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that over סמלק (jasmine) one says בורא עצי בשמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב גידל said in the name of רב: over this jasmine, we say the ברכה 'Who creates fragrant trees.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ruling about which ברכת הריח to say over jasmine. The answer is the ברכה for trees, not for plants.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The basic question is whether a fragrant plant counts as an 'עץ' (tree) or an 'עשב' (plant/herb). Jasmine has a woody stem, so רב puts it in the עצי בשמים category.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Who creates fragrant trees', the ברכה over woody fragrant plants
We say a blessing over it

phrases.english: Rav Giddel said in the name of Rav:
This jasmine —
we recite over it: 'Who creates fragrant trees.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion (on the previous amud) about עצי בשמים versus עשבי בשמים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Over jasmine (סמלק) one says בורא עצי בשמים.

steps.title: Seaside spikenard also gets the blessing for fragrant trees
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that over חלפי דימא (spikenard growing by the sea) one also says בורא עצי בשמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חננאל said in the name of רב: over these sea-reeds (spikenard), we say 'Who creates fragrant trees.'
steps.whatsHappening: A second ruling from רב adds another plant to the 'fragrant trees' list. These are reed-like plants that grow by the sea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is more surprising than jasmine, because a reed-like plant has soft stalks and does not look like a tree. That surprise sets up the next step, where a פסוק shows that soft stalks can still be called 'עץ'.

keyTerms.meaning: Sea-reeds or spikenard, reed-like fragrant plants that grow by the sea

phrases.english: Rav Chananel said in the name of Rav:
These sea-reeds (spikenard) —
we recite over them: 'Who creates fragrant trees.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second plant to the same category, from the same רב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Over seaside spikenard (חלפי דימא) one says בורא עצי בשמים.

steps.title: A verse shows that soft stalks can be called trees
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא brings a פסוק in יהושע: flax stalks are called 'פשתי העץ', so a soft-stalked plant can still count as an 'עץ'.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא said: what is the verse that supports this? 'And she brought them up to the roof and hid them in the stalks of flax of the tree' (יהושע ב:ו).
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא gives a פסוק that backs up רב's ruling. Even soft, reed-like plants can be called 'עץ', so they get עצי בשמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the story of רחב, the flax stalks she hid the spies under are called 'פשתי העץ'. Flax is soft, yet the פסוק calls it 'עץ'. This shows that 'עץ' in this context does not need a hard trunk, which supports the ruling on חלפי דימא.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the verse (that supports this)?
'Flax of the tree', meaning flax stalks

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the פסוק is about smell or ברכות. It is only used to show how the word 'עץ' can be used, so that soft stalks can count as 'trees'.

phrases.english: Mar Zutra said: What is the verse (for this)?
'And she brought them up to the roof
and hid them in the stalks of flax (literally: 'flax of the tree').'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a source from the פסוק for רב's ruling that soft-stalked plants count as עצים.
steps.raayaObject: That reed-like plants such as חלפי דימא can be called 'עץ' and get בורא עצי בשמים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: יהושע ב:ו — 'ותטמנם בפשתי העץ': flax stalks are called 'עץ'.

steps.title: Garden daffodil versus wild daffodil
steps.stepSummary: רב משרשיא rules that a garden נרקום gets בורא עצי בשמים, while a wild one from the field gets בורא עשבי בשמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב משרשיא said: over a garden daffodil we say 'Who creates fragrant trees'. Over a field (wild) daffodil we say 'Who creates fragrant plants.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ruling where the same kind of flower gets different ברכות depending on where it grows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A garden daffodil is tended and grows a firmer, woodier stem, so it is treated like a tree. A wild one stays soft and herb-like, so it gets the ברכה for plants. The species stays the same; only how it grows decides the ברכה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Who creates fragrant plants', the ברכה over herb-like fragrant plants

phrases.english: Rav Mesharshiya said:
This daffodil of the garden —
we recite over it: 'Who creates fragrant trees.'
(A daffodil) of the field: 'Who creates fragrant plants.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of rulings, now showing that where a plant grows can change its ברכה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A garden נרקום gets בורא עצי בשמים; a wild נרקום gets בורא עשבי בשמים.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the ברכה depends on the plant's actual nature as it grows, not just its name.

steps.title: Violets get the blessing for fragrant plants
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת rules that over סיגלי (violets) one says בורא עשבי בשמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: over these violets, we say 'Who creates fragrant plants.'
steps.whatsHappening: Another ruling, this time about violets, puts them in the 'fragrant plants' category.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Violets are soft, low-growing flowers with no woody stem, so they clearly fall under עשבי בשמים.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said: These violets —
we recite over them: 'Who creates fragrant plants.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another example, this one in the עשבי בשמים category.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Over violets one says בורא עשבי בשמים.

steps.title: Smelling an אתרוג or quince gets the fruit blessing
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא rules that one who smells an אתרוג or a quince says 'ברוך שנתן ריח טוב בפירות'.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא said: someone who smells an אתרוג or a quince says, 'Blessed is He Who gave a good scent to fruits.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves from flowers to fruits and gives a third type of ברכת הריח, used for fragrant fruits.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A fruit is not a 'tree' or a 'plant' in the sense of the earlier ברכות, because it is the edible part of the tree. So it gets its own ברכה that praises הקב"ה for putting a good smell into fruit.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Who gave a good scent to fruits', the ברכה over fragrant fruit

steps.whatToRemember: There are three ברכות over scent so far: בורא עצי בשמים for woody plants, בורא עשבי בשמים for soft plants, and הנותן ריח טוב בפירות for fruits.

phrases.english: Mar Zutra said:
One who smells
an etrog or a quince says:
'Blessed is He Who gave a good scent to fruits.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from fragrant plants to fragrant fruits, which get a different ברכה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Over a fragrant fruit like אתרוג or quince one says שנתן ריח טוב בפירות.

steps.title: The blessing over blossoming trees in ניסן
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה rules that one who goes out in ניסן and sees trees blossoming says a special ברכה praising הקב"ה for a world lacking nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: someone who goes out in the days of ניסן and sees trees blossoming says: 'Blessed is He Who left nothing lacking in His world, and created in it good creatures and good trees for people to enjoy.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a related ברכה. It is said over seeing blossoming trees in spring, not over smelling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a ברכת הראייה, a ברכה over a sight, not a ברכת הנהנין. It fits here because it is also about trees and enjoying הקב"ה's creation. This is the source for the well-known ברכת האילנות.

keyTerms.meaning: Who left nothing lacking in His world
To enjoy or take pleasure in

steps.confusionAlert: This ברכה is over seeing the blossoms, not smelling them. It is a different kind of ברכה from the scent ברכות before it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source of ברכת האילנות, which people still say each spring.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
One who goes out in the days of Nisan
and sees trees that are blossoming, says:
'Blessed is He Who left nothing lacking in His world

phrases.aramaic: וּבָרָא בּוֹ בְּרִיּוֹת טוֹבוֹת וְאִילָנוֹת טוֹבוֹת
phrases.english: and created in it good creatures and good trees
for people to enjoy them.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a related topic, a ברכה over the sight of blossoming trees.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who sees trees blossoming in ניסן says ברוך שלא חיסר בעולמו כלום.

steps.title: What is the source for blessing over scent?
steps.stepSummary: רב זוטרא בר טוביה, in the name of רב, asks where we learn that one must say a ברכה over smell.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב זוטרא בר טוביה said in the name of רב: from where do we know that we say a ברכה over a good smell?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of ברכת הריח. This line sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually we bless over what we eat or drink, which the body enjoys. Smell is not eaten, so it is fair to ask why it needs a ברכה at all.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב זוּטְרָא בַּר טוֹבִיָּה אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rav Zutra bar Toviya said in the name of Rav:
From where do we know that we bless over scent?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the main topic of ברכת הריח and asks for its basic source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source in the פסוקים that requires a ברכה over scent.

steps.title: Scent is what the soul enjoys and the body does not
steps.stepSummary: The source is 'כל הנשמה תהלל יה'. Scent is the one thing the נשמה enjoys without the body, so the נשמה must praise הקב"ה for it.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'Let every soul praise God' (תהלים קנ:ו). What is something the soul enjoys and the body does not? You must say: that is scent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a פסוק. It explains that the 'נשמה' in the פסוק points to scent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the 'נשמה' should praise הקב"ה. Eating and drinking feed the body, but smell gives pleasure without feeding the body at all. So it is the pleasure of the נשמה, and it still needs a ברכה.

keyTerms.meaning: You must say (the only possible answer is)

steps.whatToRemember: We bless over smell because of 'כל הנשמה תהלל יה'. Scent is the pleasure of the נשמה, not of the body.

phrases.english: As it says: 'Let every soul praise God.'
What is a thing that the soul enjoys
and the body does not enjoy?
You must say: that is scent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8 with a פסוק and its explanation.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'כל הנשמה תהלל יה' requires a ברכה over scent, because scent is enjoyed by the נשמה alone.
steps.whyThisMatters: It explains why ברכת הריח exists at all, even though nothing is eaten.

steps.title: The young men of ישראל will give off a fragrance like the לבנון
steps.stepSummary: רב זוטרא בר טוביה, in the name of רב, teaches as אגדה that in the future the young men of ישראל will give off a good scent like the לבנון, based on a פסוק in הושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב זוטרא בר טוביה said in the name of רב: in the future, the young men of ישראל will give off a good scent like the לבנון. As it says: 'His branches will spread, his beauty will be like the olive tree, and his fragrance like the לבנון' (הושע יד:ז).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second teaching from the same speaker. It is an אגדה about a good scent in the future.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is placed here because it shares the theme of a good smell and comes from the same חכם. The 'young branches' (יונקותיו) in the פסוק are read as the young men of ישראל, whose fragrance will be like the לבנון.

keyTerms.meaning: Like the לבנון (famous for its fragrant cedars)

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב זוּטְרָא בַּר טוֹבִיָּה אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: And Rav Zutra bar Toviya said in the name of Rav:
The young men of Israel are destined
to give off a good scent like the Lebanon.
As it says: 'His young branches will spread,
and his beauty will be like the olive tree,
and his fragrance like the Lebanon.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב זוּטְרָא בַּר טוֹבִיָּה אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second teaching by the same speaker, linked by the shared theme of good scent.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the future the young men of ישראל will give off a fragrance like the לבנון, based on הושע יד:ז.

steps.title: Everyone is made to love his own trade
steps.stepSummary: רב זוטרא בר טוביה, quoting רב, explains the פסוק 'את הכל עשה יפה בעתו' to mean that הקב"ה makes each person's work pleasant in his own eyes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב זוטרא בר טוביה said in the name of רב: What does the פסוק 'He has made everything beautiful in its time' mean? It teaches that הקב"ה made each person's trade pleasant to him in his own eyes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds another teaching from the same chain, רב זוטרא בר טוביה quoting רב. This one explains a פסוק in קהלת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'beautiful in its time' are read as being about how people see their work. הקב"ה makes each person happy with his own trade. That way every job in the world gets done, even jobs that others find unpleasant.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the meaning of what is written (introduces an explanation of a פסוק)
In his own eyes (literally: before his face)

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב זוּטְרָא בַּר טוֹבִיָּה אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: And Rav Zutra bar Toviya said that Rav said:
What is the meaning of that which is written
"He has made everything beautiful in its time"
This teaches that each and every person,
the Holy One, Blessed be He, made pleasant for him
his own trade, in his own eyes.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב זוּטְרָא בַּר טוֹבִיָּה אָמַר רַב: מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another teaching in the series of sayings from רב זוטרא בר טוביה in the name of רב. It is not connected in content to step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הקב"ה makes each person's trade pleasant in his own eyes, as taught by 'את הכל עשה יפה בעתו'.

steps.title: A folk saying that matches the teaching
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא connects the teaching to a popular saying: hang a palm delicacy on a pig and it will still do what pigs do.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: This is what people say: 'Hang a palm heart on a pig, and it will still do its own thing.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא supports רב's teaching with a well-known saying. Every creature keeps to its own nature and taste.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Give a pig a fancy treat and it will still roll it in the mud, because that is what it likes. People are the same. What looks unpleasant to one person is enjoyable to another, so you cannot judge someone else's work by your own taste.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what people say (introduces a popular saying)
Heart of the palm tree, a delicacy
'Something else', a polite way of saying 'pig'

steps.confusionAlert: 'דבר אחר' here does not mean 'another explanation' as it usually does. In this saying it is a polite way of saying 'pig'.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
This is what people say:
"Hang a heart of palm on a pig ('the other thing'),
and it will still do its own thing."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up step 11 with a matching popular saying.
steps.raayaObject: The idea that each person finds his own work pleasant.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The saying that a pig keeps its own habits even when given a delicacy.

steps.title: A torch counts like two, and the moon like three
steps.stepSummary: רב זוטרא בר טוביה, quoting רב, teaches that for someone walking at night, a torch protects like having two people, and moonlight like having three.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב זוטרא בר טוביה said in the name of רב: A torch is like two, and the moon is like three.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching from the same chain. It is about how much protection a person has from danger (מזיקין) when walking alone at night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Going out alone at night carries danger. Light gives protection, as if more people were with you. A torch counts as two people, and moonlight counts as three.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב זוּטְרָא בַּר טוֹבִיָּה אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: And Rav Zutra bar Toviya said that Rav said:
A torch is like two,
and the moon is like three.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב זוּטְרָא בַּר טוֹבִיָּה אָמַר רַב: אֲבוּקָה כִּשְׁנַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new, unrelated teaching in the same series of sayings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For protection at night, a torch counts like two people and moonlight like three.

steps.title: Does 'two' include the person himself?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether 'a torch is like two' means the walker plus the torch, or two people in addition to the walker.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: Is a torch like two including the person, or perhaps like two besides him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a question of meaning about רב's words. It sets up a proof that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two ways to read it. In the first, the torch makes him like two people in total. In the second, the torch is like two extra people, so three in total. The phrase 'a torch is like two' alone does not tell us which. The next step answers this from the other half of רב's own teaching.

phrases.english: They asked:
Is a torch like two including him,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִילְמָא אֲבוּקָה כִּשְׁנַיִם לְבַר מִדִּידֵיהּ?
phrases.english: or perhaps a torch is like two besides him?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how to understand the numbers in step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the count of 'two' includes the walker himself or is in addition to him.

steps.title: Proof from the moon: four would be pointless
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves the answer from 'the moon is like three'. If it meant three besides him, that would be four, but more than three adds nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'And the moon is like three.' If you say this includes him, that works well. But if you say it is besides him, why would I need four? Didn't the Master say: To one person a demon is seen and harms; to two it is seen but does not harm; to three it is not seen at all?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a proof using the second half of רב's teaching about the moon. It shows that the 'besides him' reading does not make sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An earlier teaching says that with three people, danger is not even seen, so three is full protection. If the moon meant three besides him, it would equal four people, and a fourth adds nothing. So the numbers must include the person himself.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't the Master say? (brings in a known teaching)

phrases.english: Come and hear: "And the moon is like three."

phrases.aramaic: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא בַּהֲדֵי דִידֵיהּ — שַׁפִּיר.
phrases.english: Granted, if you say it includes him, that works well.
But if you say it is besides him,
why do I need four?
But didn't the Master say:
To one person, a demon is seen and causes harm;
to two, it is seen but does not cause harm;
to three, it is not seen at all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14 using the second half of רב's teaching in step 13.
steps.raayaObject: The reading that the count includes the person himself.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The moon equals three, combined with the known teaching that three is full protection, so a fourth would be pointless.

steps.title: Conclusion: the count includes the person
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that 'a torch is like two' means two including the person himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, isn't it proven from here that a torch is like two including him? Yes, it is proven.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the question with a firm conclusion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the moon's 'three' must include the person, the torch's 'two' also includes him. So a person with a torch is protected like two people walking together.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, is it not so that

steps.whatToRemember: A torch makes a lone walker like two people, and moonlight like three, counting the walker himself.

phrases.english: Rather, isn't it proven from this
that a torch is like two including him?
Yes, it is proven.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the final conclusion from the proof in step 15.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: 'A torch is like two' includes the person himself.

steps.title: Better a fiery furnace than shaming someone in public
steps.stepSummary: A teaching with three possible sources: a person should rather throw himself into a fiery furnace than embarrass another person in public.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב זוטרא בר טוביה said in the name of רב (and some say רב חנא בר ביזנא in the name of רבי שמעון חסידא, and some say רבי יוחנן in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחי): It is better for a person to throw himself into a fiery furnace than to whiten the face of his friend in public.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a final teaching from this chain. It records three different versions of who said it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Whitening the face' describes how a person goes pale when shamed. The teaching treats public embarrassment as so terrible that it is better to suffer burning than to cause it.

keyTerms.meaning: It is better for a person
Whiten his friend's face (shame him until he goes pale)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a basic source for how serious it is to embarrass someone in public (הלבנת פנים).

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב זוּטְרָא בַּר טוֹבִיָּה אָמַר רַב,
phrases.english: And Rav Zutra bar Toviya said that Rav said;

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ אָמַר רַב חָנָא בַּר בִּיזְנָא
phrases.english: and some say Rav Chana bar Bizna said
that Rabbi Shimon Chasida said;
and some say Rabbi Yochanan said
in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai:
It is better for a person
to throw himself into a fiery furnace
than to whiten the face of his friend in public.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב זוּטְרָא בַּר טוֹבִיָּה אָמַר רַב, וְאָמְרִי לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new, unrelated teaching in the same series of sayings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: It is better to throw oneself into a fiery furnace than to embarrass another person in public.

steps.title: Where do we learn this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of the teaching against public embarrassment.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a source. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Such an extreme statement needs a source. The גמרא asks for one before accepting it.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know this?

phrases.english: From where do we derive this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the teaching in step 17.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The biblical source for preferring death over shaming someone in public.

steps.title: The source is תמר
steps.stepSummary: The source is תמר. While being taken out to be burned, she did not openly name יהודה and left it to him to admit the truth.
steps.simpleTranslation: From תמר, as it is said: 'As she was being brought out...'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with the story of תמר and יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תמר was being taken out to be burned. She could have saved herself by announcing that יהודה was the father. Instead she only sent his items and said 'whose are these?', so he could admit it himself. She was ready to be burned rather than shame him in public.

keyTerms.meaning: As she was being brought out (to be burned)
And so on (the rest of the פסוק)

steps.whatToRemember: Embarrassing someone in public is so serious that תמר was ready to be burned rather than shame יהודה.

phrases.english: From Tamar,
as it is stated: "As she was being brought out, and so on."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: תמר chose to face burning rather than publicly name יהודה, as the פסוק 'היא מוצאת' shows.

steps.title: Oil and myrtle: which blessing comes first
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records a מחלוקת between בית שמאי and בית הלל about whether to bless first on fragrant oil or on myrtle.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: If someone was brought scented oil and myrtle, בית שמאי say he blesses on the oil first and then on the myrtle. בית הלל say he blesses on the myrtle first and then on the oil.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting a ברייתא. בית שמאי and בית הלל disagree about the order of the smell-blessings when a person has both oil and myrtle in front of him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions agree that each item gets its own blessing. They argue only about which item is more important and therefore comes first. בית שמאי put oil first, and בית הלל put myrtle first.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
If they brought before him oil and myrtle,
Beit Shammai say:
He blesses on the oil
and afterward he blesses on the myrtle.
And Beit Hillel say:
He blesses on the myrtle
and afterward he blesses on the oil.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הֵבִיאוּ לְפָנָיו שֶׁמֶן וַהֲדַס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, the order of fragrance blessings, after the discussion of public embarrassment.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי bless on oil first. בית הלל bless on myrtle first.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל decides for oil
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל settles the dispute in favor of oil first, because oil has two uses (smell and anointing) while myrtle has only one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן גמליאל said: I will decide. With oil, we benefit from its smell and from smearing it on the body. With myrtle, we benefit from its smell, but we cannot smear it on.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן גמליאל steps in as a decider and sides with בית שמאי that oil comes first. He gives a reason for his decision.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His logic is that the item with more benefit is more important. Oil gives two kinds of benefit, smell and anointing. Myrtle gives only smell, so oil should get the first blessing.

keyTerms.meaning: I will decide (literally, tip the scales)
We have the privilege of, we benefit from

steps.confusionAlert: Usually we follow בית הלל. Here רבן גמליאל, the decider, actually sides with בית שמאי that oil comes first.

phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel said: I will decide.
Oil: we benefit from its smell
and we benefit from anointing with it.
Myrtle: we benefit from its smell,
but we do not benefit from anointing with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the dispute in step 20 with a reasoned decision.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Oil comes first because it has two benefits while myrtle has only one.

steps.title: The הלכה follows the decider
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that the הלכה follows רבן גמליאל, so one blesses on oil first.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: The הלכה is like the words of the one who decided.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives the practical ruling for this dispute. We follow רבן גמליאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This turns רבן גמליאל's opinion into practical הלכה. In practice, a person blesses on the oil first, even though that matches בית שמאי.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who decides between two opinions

steps.whatToRemember: Oil comes before myrtle, because הלכה follows רבן גמליאל, the decider.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
The halacha is like the words of the decider.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: הֲלָכָה כְּדִבְרֵי הַמַּכְרִיעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns רבן גמליאל's decision into practical הלכה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: One blesses on oil before myrtle.

steps.title: רב פפא blesses on the myrtle first
steps.stepSummary: A story: רב פפא visits רב הונא בריה דרב איקא and blesses on the myrtle before the oil.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא happened to come to the house of רב הונא son of רב איקא. They brought oil and myrtle before them. רב פפא took the myrtle and blessed on it first, and then blessed on the oil.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story where רב פפא seems to act against רבי יוחנן's ruling. This sets up the next step, where he is challenged.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By blessing on the myrtle first, רב פפא followed the order of בית הלל and not the decider. This creates the tension the next steps deal with.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa happened to come

phrases.aramaic: לְבֵי רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא.
phrases.english: to the house of Rav Huna son of Rav Ika.
They brought before them oil and myrtle.

phrases.aramaic: שְׁקַל רַב פָּפָּא בָּרֵיךְ אַהֲדַס בְּרֵישָׁא,
phrases.english: Rav Pappa took and blessed on the myrtle first,
and then blessed on the oil.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא אִיקְּלַע לְבֵי רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a story that seems to contradict the ruling of step 22.

steps.title: רב הונא challenges רב פפא
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא asks רב פפא why he did not follow the ruling that הלכה is like the decider.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Doesn't the Master hold that the הלכה is like the words of the decider?
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא challenges רב פפא's action. The question form here is really an objection.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן ruled like רבן גמליאל, which means oil comes first. רב פפא did the opposite, so his behavior seems to go against the accepted ruling.

phrases.english: He said to him:
Does the Master not hold
that the halacha is like the words of the decider?

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא סָבַר לַהּ מָר הֲלָכָה כְּדִבְרֵי הַמַּכְרִיעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב פפא's action from step 23 using the ruling of step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's blessing on the myrtle first
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן ruled like the decider, who puts oil first. רב פפא's order contradicts that ruling.

steps.title: רב פפא cites רבא
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers that רבא ruled like בית הלל, who put myrtle first.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: This is what רבא said: The הלכה is like בית הלל.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא defends himself by quoting a ruling from רבא that supports what he did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבא really ruled like בית הלל, then blessing on the myrtle first would be correct. That would justify רב פפא's order.

phrases.english: He said to him: Rava said thus:
The halacha is like Beit Hillel.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לֵיהּ: הָכִי אָמַר רָבָא: הֲלָכָה כְּבֵית הִלֵּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 24.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב פפא acted against the accepted ruling.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב פפא claims he followed רבא, who ruled like בית הלל.

steps.title: רב פפא was only getting out of an awkward spot
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects רב פפא's claim. רבא never said it, and רב פפא said it only to cover himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: But that is not so. He did it only to get himself out of the situation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא itself comments that רב פפא's answer was not a real ruling of רבא. He used it to cover for his mistake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This cancels the answer from step 25. The ruling of רבי יוחנן stays in place, and oil comes before myrtle.

keyTerms.meaning: To slip out of it, to excuse himself

steps.confusionAlert: Do not take step 25 as real הלכה. The גמרא says רבא never ruled like בית הלל here, so the הלכה is still oil first.
steps.whatToRemember: The story does not change the ruling. One still blesses on oil before myrtle.

phrases.english: But it is not so;
he did it in order to extricate himself.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא הִיא, לְאִשְׁתְּמוֹטֵי נַפְשֵׁיהּ הוּא דַּעֲבַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Overturns the answer of step 25 and closes the story.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that רבא ruled like בית הלל
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: No such ruling existed. It was only an excuse.

steps.title: Oil and wine according to בית שמאי
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא: with oil and wine, בית שמאי say to hold the oil in the right hand and bless on it first.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: If they brought oil and wine before them, בית שמאי say he holds the oil in his right hand and the wine in his left. He blesses on the oil and then blesses on the wine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא about a related case, oil together with wine. This step gives בית שמאי's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The more important item goes in the right hand and is blessed first. בית שמאי treat oil as the more important item.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
If they brought before them oil and wine,
Beit Shammai say:
He holds the oil in his right hand
and the wine in his left,
he blesses on the oil
and then blesses on the wine.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הֵבִיאוּ לִפְנֵיהֶם שֶׁמֶן וְיַיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel ברייתא about a new pair of items, oil and wine.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי: oil in the right hand, blessed first.

steps.title: Oil and wine according to בית הלל
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל say to hold the wine in the right hand and bless on it first, then wipe the oil on the servant's head.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית הלל say he holds the wine in his right hand and the oil in his left. He blesses on the wine and then on the oil, and he wipes the oil on the servant's head.
steps.whatsHappening: This step gives בית הלל's opposite view. It also adds what to do with the leftover oil on his hands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For בית הלל, wine is more important, so it goes in the right hand and is blessed first. He wipes the extra oil on the servant's head so his own hands do not stay perfumed.

phrases.english: Beit Hillel say:
He holds the wine in his right hand
and the oil in his left,
he blesses on the wine
and then blesses on the oil,
and he smears it on the head of the servant.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים: אוֹחֵז אֶת הַיַּיִן בִּימִינוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to בית שמאי in step 27.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית הלל: wine in the right hand, blessed first. The leftover oil is smeared on the servant's head.

steps.title: If the servant is a Torah scholar
steps.stepSummary: If the servant is a תלמיד חכם, he wipes the oil on the wall instead, because a תלמיד חכם should not go out perfumed.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the servant is a תלמיד חכם, he wipes the oil on the wall, because it is a disgrace for a תלמיד חכם to go out to the market perfumed.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds an exception to the servant rule. This also sets up the next ברייתא about improper conduct for a תלמיד חכם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the oil goes on the servant's head. If the servant is a scholar, putting perfume on him would cause him disgrace in public, so the wall is used instead.

phrases.english: And if the servant is a Torah scholar,
he smears it on the wall,
because it is a disgrace for a Torah scholar
to go out to the market when he is perfumed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds an exception to the servant rule in step 28.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the servant is a scholar, the oil is wiped on the wall.

steps.title: Six things unbecoming for a Torah scholar
steps.stepSummary: Following the mention of what is disgraceful for a scholar, a ברייתא lists six improper behaviors for a תלמיד חכם.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: Six things are a disgrace for a תלמיד חכם. He should not go out perfumed to the market. He should not go out alone at night. He should not go out in patched shoes. He should not talk with a woman in the market. He should not recline at a meal with a group of עמי הארץ. He should not be the last to enter the בית המדרש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves off topic. Since it just mentioned something disgraceful for a תלמיד חכם, it brings a list of six such things.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first item, going out perfumed, links this list to the previous step. The other items are about a scholar's dignity, reputation, and avoiding suspicion.
steps.whyThisMatters: A תלמיד חכם represents the Torah. His behavior in public reflects on the Torah's honor.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:

phrases.aramaic: שִׁשָּׁה דְּבָרִים גְּנַאי לוֹ לְתַלְמִיד חָכָם:
phrases.english: Six things are a disgrace for a Torah scholar:
He should not go out perfumed to the market;
and he should not go out alone at night;
and he should not go out in patched shoes;
and he should not converse with a woman in the market;

phrases.aramaic: וְאַל יָסֵב בַּחֲבוּרָה שֶׁל עַמֵּי הָאָרֶץ,
phrases.english: and he should not recline in a group of ignoramuses;
and he should not enter last to the study hall.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: שִׁשָּׁה דְּבָרִים גְּנַאי לוֹ לְתַלְמִיד חָכָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side topic triggered by the mention in step 29 of what is disgraceful for a scholar.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Six behaviors are unbecoming for a תלמיד חכם.

steps.title: Some add two more improper behaviors
steps.stepSummary: A second opinion, the יש אומרים, adds that a scholar should not take large strides or walk with an overly upright posture.
steps.simpleTranslation: And some say: He should also not take large steps, and he should not walk with an upright, proud posture.
steps.whatsHappening: A different opinion adds two more items to the list of things unbecoming for a תלמיד חכם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both additions are about how a scholar walks. Big strides look rushed and undignified, and walking too upright looks arrogant.
steps.whatToRemember: A תלמיד חכם must guard his dignity and humility in how he looks, walks, and behaves in public.

phrases.english: And some say:
Also he should not take a large stride,
and he should not walk with an upright posture.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְיֵשׁ אוֹמְרִים: אַף לֹא יַפְסִיעַ פְּסִיעָה גַּסָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds two items to the list in step 30.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A scholar should not take large strides or walk with a haughty posture.

steps.title: Going out perfumed applies only where people are suspected of immorality
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the first item of the ברייתא, going out perfumed. In the name of רבי יוחנן, it limits the rule to a place where people are suspected of מִשְׁכַּב זָכוּר.
steps.simpleTranslation: "He should not go out perfumed to the marketplace." רבי אבא, the son of רבי חייא בר אבא, said in the name of רבי יוחנן: this applies in a place where people are suspected of homosexual relations.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts explaining the ברייתא line by line. First it explains why a scholar should not go out perfumed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Perfume by itself is not the problem. The problem is the suspicion it can cause: where such behavior is common, a perfumed man may be suspected of trying to attract men. So the rule is limited to those places.

phrases.english: He should not go out perfumed to the marketplace:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא
phrases.english: Rabbi Abba, son of Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba, said
that Rabbi Yochanan said:
in a place where they are suspected of homosexual relations.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts explaining the ברייתא items listed in step 30
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Going out perfumed is improper only where people are suspected of מִשְׁכַּב זָכוּר

steps.title: Perfume on clothing is a problem, but perfume on the body is not
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת limits the perfume rule to clothing. On the body, sweat makes the scent fade.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: we only said this about perfume on his clothing. But on his body, sweat makes the scent go away.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת narrows the perfume rule further. It applies only when the perfume is on his clothes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Perfume on clothing stays strong and is noticed by people around him. Perfume on the skin fades quickly because of sweat. So it does not create the same suspicion.

keyTerms.meaning: We only said this in the case of... (a limiting formula)

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:
We only said this regarding his clothing,
but regarding his body —
sweat makes it go away.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת לָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא בְּבִגְדוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a limitation to the perfume rule
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only perfumed clothing is a problem; perfume on the body fades

steps.title: Is hair like clothing or like the body?
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says hair is treated like clothing. A second version of his statement says hair is treated like the body.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: his hair is like his clothing. Some say he said: his hair is like his body.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא decides which side of רב ששת's line perfumed hair falls on. Two versions of his statement are reported.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the first version, scent stays in hair, so perfumed hair is a problem. According to the second version, hair is part of the body, where the scent fades, so it is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Is similar to, is treated like

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
And his hair is like his clothing,
and some say: it is like his body.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא וּשְׂעָרוֹ כְּבִגְדוֹ דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies רב ששת's distinction to hair
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Hair is like clothing, or by the second version, like the body

steps.title: Not going out alone at night, because of suspicion
steps.stepSummary: The second item of the ברייתא: a scholar should not go out alone at night, because people may suspect him.
steps.simpleTranslation: "He should not go out alone at night": because of suspicion.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next item in the ברייתא and gives its reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A man walking alone at night may be suspected of going to an improper meeting. A scholar must protect his reputation, so he should avoid this.

phrases.english: And he should not go out alone at night:
because of suspicion.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next item in the ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Going out alone at night is improper because of suspicion

steps.title: A scholar with a fixed study time may go out at night
steps.stepSummary: The rule applies only if he has no fixed time. If he has a set time to go learn, everyone knows where he is going.
steps.simpleTranslation: We only said this when he has no fixed time. But if he has a fixed time, it is well known that he is going at his usual time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא limits the night rule. It does not apply to someone with a known, regular schedule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole rule is based on suspicion. When people know he goes every night at a set time to learn, they have no reason to suspect him, so the reason for the rule falls away.

phrases.english: And we only said this
when he has no fixed time,
but if he has a fixed time —
it is well known that he is going for his set time.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא דְּלָא קְבִיעַ לֵיהּ עִידָּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the rule of step 35
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone with a known fixed time may go out alone at night

steps.title: The patched shoes rule supports רבי חייא בר אבא
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא's item about patched shoes supports רבי חייא בר אבא, who said it is a disgrace for a scholar to go out in patched shoes.
steps.simpleTranslation: "He should not go out in patched shoes": this supports רבי חייא בר אבא, who said: it is a disgrace for a תלמיד חכם to go out in patched shoes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that this line of the ברייתא backs up an אמורא's statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חייא בר אבא said the same rule on his own. The ברייתא now shows that an older source agrees with him.

phrases.english: And he should not go out in patched shoes:

phrases.aramaic: מְסַיַּיע לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא.
phrases.english: This supports Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba.
For Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said:
It is a disgrace for a Torah scholar
to go out in patched shoes.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְסַיַּיע לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next item in the ברייתא and links it to an אמורא
steps.raayaObject: רבי חייא בר אבא's statement that patched shoes are a disgrace for a scholar
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's list of improper behaviors for a scholar

steps.title: But רבי חייא בר אבא himself wore patched shoes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: how can this be, if רבי חייא בר אבא himself went out in patched shoes?
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that really so? But רבי חייא בר אבא himself went out in patched shoes!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a contradiction between what רבי חייא בר אבא taught and what he did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If going out in patched shoes is a disgrace, a great scholar would not do it himself. His behavior seems to show that the rule is not absolute.

phrases.english: Is that so?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא נָפֵיק!
phrases.english: But Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba went out (in them)!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי וְהָא רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא נָפֵיק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the statement supported in step 37
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חייא בר אבא's rule against patched shoes
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His own conduct contradicts his teaching

steps.title: The disgrace is only a patch on top of a patch
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא answers that the rule is about shoes with a patch on top of another patch. A single patch is fine.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא, the son of רב נחמן, said: the rule is about a patch on top of a patch.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction by making the rule narrower.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חייא בר אבא wore shoes with a single patch, which is acceptable. Only a patch sewn over another patch looks shabby enough to disgrace a scholar.

keyTerms.meaning: A patch on top of a patch

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר מָר זוּטְרָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן:
phrases.english: Mar Zutra, son of Rav Nachman, said:
(It refers to) a patch on top of a patch.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר זוּטְרָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן בִּטְלַאי עַל גַּבֵּי טְלַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 38
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any patched shoe is a disgrace
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a double patch is a disgrace; רבי חייא בר אבא wore a single patch

steps.title: Only patches on the upper part of the shoe count
steps.stepSummary: The rule applies to patches on the upper part of the shoe, not on the sole.
steps.simpleTranslation: We only said this about the upper part of the shoe. On the sole, we have no problem with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds another limit: the patch must be on the visible upper part of the shoe.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Patches on the sole are hidden under the foot, so nobody sees them. Only a visible patch makes the scholar look shabby.

keyTerms.meaning: The upper part of the shoe
The sole (leather bottom) of the shoe
We have no problem with it

phrases.english: And we only said this about the upper part,
but on the sole — we have no problem with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a further limit to the patched shoes rule
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only patches on the upper part of the shoe are a disgrace

steps.title: Only on the road, not at home
steps.stepSummary: Even patches on the upper part are a problem only when he goes out on the road, not inside his house.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even on the upper part, we only said this on the road. But at home, we have no problem with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a third limit: the rule applies only in public.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The disgrace is about how the public sees the scholar. At home no one sees him, so there is no disgrace.

phrases.english: And regarding the upper part, we only said this on the road,
but at home — we have no problem with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Further limits the rule from step 40
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Upper patches are only a problem in public

steps.title: Only in the summer, not in the rainy season
steps.stepSummary: The rule applies only in the summer. In the rainy season, mud covers the patches.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we only said this in the summer. But in the rainy season, we have no problem with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a final limit to the patched shoes rule: it depends on the season.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the rainy season the shoes are covered with mud, so the patches cannot be seen. In summer they are clearly visible.
steps.whatToRemember: The patched shoes rule is very narrow: a double patch, on the upper part, in public, in summer. Every limit follows the same idea, that the problem is a visible, shabby look.

phrases.english: And we only said this in the summer,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל בִּימוֹת הַגְּשָׁמִים — לֵית לַן בַּהּ.
phrases.english: but in the rainy season — we have no problem with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final limit on the patched shoes rule
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Patched shoes are only a problem in summer, when the patches are visible

steps.title: No talking with a woman in the marketplace, even his wife
steps.stepSummary: The next item of the ברייתא: a scholar should not talk with a woman in the marketplace. רב חסדא says this applies even to his own wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: "He should not talk with a woman in the marketplace." רב חסדא said: even if she is his wife.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next item in the ברייתא, and רב חסדא extends it even to the scholar's own wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A beginner might think a man's own wife is surely allowed. רב חסדא says no, because onlookers do not know who she is and may suspect him.

phrases.english: And he should not converse with a woman in the marketplace:
Rav Chisda said:
Even if she is his wife.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next item in the ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A scholar should not talk with any woman in the marketplace, even his wife

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רב חסדא and adds daughter and sister
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches the same rule: even with his wife, daughter, or sister, because not everyone knows who his relatives are.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא also teaches this: even if she is his wife, his daughter, or his sister, because not everyone knows who his female relatives are.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports רב חסדא and explains the reason for the rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא confirms רב חסדא's ruling and extends it to close relatives. The reason is that people in the market do not know which women are his relatives, so they may suspect him.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way in a ברייתא

steps.whatToRemember: Several items on the list share the same reason: a תלמיד חכם must avoid anything that could cause people to suspect him, even when he is doing nothing wrong.

phrases.english: It was also taught this way:
even if she is his wife,
and even if she is his daughter,
and even if she is his sister —
because not everyone knows who his female relatives are.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב חסדא's ruling with a ברייתא
steps.raayaObject: רב חסדא's ruling that the rule applies even to his wife
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that includes his wife, daughter, and sister

steps.title: Why not eat with ignorant people?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next item of the ברייתא, that a scholar should not eat in a group of עמי הארץ, and asks for the reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: "He should not recline at a meal with a group of ignorant people." What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next rule from the ברייתא and asks why it is so. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gave the rule without a reason. The גמרא's question looks for the concern behind it, so we understand what danger a תלמיד חכם faces at such a meal.

keyTerms.meaning: Recline at a meal, meaning join a formal meal
A group or company, here people eating together
Ignorant people who are not careful in תורה and מצוות

phrases.english: And he should not recline in a group
phrases.notes: Quoting the next item in the ברייתא

phrases.english: of ignorant people.
What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next item in the same ברייתא list after finishing the item about speaking with women.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason a תלמיד חכם should not eat with עמי הארץ.

steps.title: He might be drawn after them
steps.stepSummary: The reason is that he might be pulled into following their ways.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps he will come to be drawn after them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. The concern is that the scholar will be influenced and start acting like them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem is not the meal itself. It is the social pull of the company: sitting closely with people who are not careful can slowly change how a scholar acts.

keyTerms.meaning: To be drawn after them, meaning to follow their ways

phrases.english: Perhaps he will come
to be drawn after them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 45.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The concern is that he will be influenced to follow their behavior.

steps.title: Do not be the last one into the study hall
steps.stepSummary: A scholar should not be the last to enter the בית המדרש, because people will call him a פושע, meaning lazy and careless.
steps.simpleTranslation: "He should not be the last to enter the study hall," because people will call him negligent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next item of the ברייתא and immediately gives its reason. People will see him come in last and call him lazy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the concern is reputation, not influence. A תלמיד חכם who always arrives last looks like he does not care about learning, and that lowers the honor of Torah.

phrases.english: And he should not enter last
into the study hall.
Because they will call him "negligent."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next item in the same ברייתא list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A תלמיד חכם should not be the last to enter the בית המדרש, so that he is not seen as lazy.

steps.title: Some say: no long strides, because they harm eyesight
steps.stepSummary: יש אומרים add that a scholar should not take long strides, because the מר taught that a long stride takes away one five-hundredth of a person's eyesight.
steps.simpleTranslation: And some say: he should also not take long strides. As the Master said: a long stride takes away one five-hundredth of a person's eyesight.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא quotes an extra opinion (יש אומרים) adding one more item to the list. The גמרא supports it with a known teaching about harm to the eyes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This item is about health and dignity, not reputation. Hurrying with big, rushed steps is undignified, and the teaching of the מר adds that it physically weakens a person's sight.

keyTerms.meaning: The light of his eyes, meaning his eyesight

phrases.english: And some say,
he should also not take long strides.
As the Master said,
a long stride takes away
one five-hundredth
of a person's eyesight.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְיֵשׁ אוֹמְרִים אַף לֹא יַפְסִיעַ פְּסִיעָה גַּסָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a further item to the list, given in the name of יש אומרים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A תלמיד חכם should not take long strides, since they damage eyesight.

steps.title: What fixes the damage?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the remedy is for someone who already took long strides.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is his remedy?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a practical question: if someone already lost some eyesight this way, how can he fix it? The answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once we learn that long strides cause damage, the natural follow-up is whether the damage can be undone.

phrases.english: What is his remedy?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follow-up question on the damage described in step 48.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How to restore the eyesight lost through long strides.

steps.title: קידוש wine on Friday night restores it
steps.stepSummary: He can restore his eyesight through the wine of קידוש on ערב שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: He can restore it with the קידוש of Friday night (by drinking its wine).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: drinking the wine of קידוש on Friday night brings back the lost eyesight.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "בי שמשי" refers to the evening when the sun sets into שבת, meaning Friday night. The remedy is tied to a מצוה: the קידוש cup repairs what the rushed walking damaged.

keyTerms.meaning: He can bring it back, restore it
The קידוש of the evening, meaning Friday night קידוש

phrases.english: He can restore it
with the Kiddush of Friday night.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 49.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Drinking the wine of Friday night קידוש restores the lost eyesight.

steps.title: Do not walk with a proud, upright posture
steps.stepSummary: A scholar should not walk fully upright, because the מר taught that walking that way even four אמות is like pushing away the feet of the שכינה.
steps.simpleTranslation: "He should not walk with an upright posture." As the מר said: one who walks with an upright posture, even four אמות, is as if he pushes away the feet of the שכינה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the last item of the ברייתא and supports it with a teaching of the מר about how serious arrogant walking is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "Upright posture" here means walking proudly with the head held high. Even a short distance of four אמות counts, because acting arrogant is like crowding out the שכינה. The source for why the שכינה is "there" comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Upright, erect posture, meaning walking proudly
Pushes away the feet of the שכינה

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean a person must walk hunched over. It is speaking against walking in a haughty, arrogant way. A slight bow shows humility.

phrases.english: And he should not walk with an upright posture.
As the Master said:
one who walks with an upright posture,
even four cubits,
it is as if he pushes away the feet of the Divine Presence,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final item of the ברייתא list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A תלמיד חכם should not walk arrogantly upright, even four אמות, because it is like pushing away the שכינה.

steps.title: Verse: the whole world is full of His glory
steps.stepSummary: The source is the פסוק "מלא כל הארץ כבודו". Since God's glory is everywhere, walking arrogantly crowds out the שכינה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: "The whole earth is full of His glory" (ישעיהו ו:ג).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק to prove the teaching of the מר. God's glory fills every place, so arrogance anywhere pushes against the שכינה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק explains why the שכינה is right where the person is walking: it fills the entire world. A proud posture shows that a person does not feel God's presence around him, and so it is as if he is pushing it away.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is written (introduces a פסוק)
The whole earth is full of His glory

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא's list closes with rules about a תלמיד חכם's company, punctuality, and walking. Each rule has its own concern: being influenced (עמי הארץ), reputation (arriving last), health (long strides), and humility before the שכינה (upright posture).

phrases.english: As it is written: "The whole earth is full of His glory."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the scriptural source for the teaching of the מר in step 51.
steps.raayaObject: That arrogant walking pushes away the שכינה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ישעיהו ו:ג, "מלא כל הארץ כבודו": God's glory is present everywhere.
